original_question: For polytopes of a fixed combinatorial type, describe the collections of sails of the associated cones arising from all such polytopes.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly focuses on collections of sails, on cones attached to a polytope, and on fixing the combinatorial type of the polytope. In fact, it is essentially a paraphrase of Section 3.3, Problem 8.
missing_details: The paper's exact target is Section 3.3, Problem 8, explicitly named the "Multidimensional IKEA problem."
The ambient setting is the real space R^n equipped with its lattice of integer points Z^n; this global lattice setting is assumed throughout Section 2 and Section 3.

The word "sail" is not informal: it refers to the general construction in Definition 2.2, which depends on a chosen pair (S, L). Problem 8 does not restrict itself to only Klein sails or only Minkowski-Voronoi sails.

The associated cones are the cones at the polytope's angles/vertices; this is the multidimensional analogue of Problem 2 on the angle data of integer n-gons, and the sentence immediately before Problem 8 frames the problem in terms of continued fractions in the different angles of a tetrahedron.

The local context is the finite/rational setting: Section 3.1 identifies rational cones as having finite sails, and the sentence just before Problem 8 explicitly speaks about finite continued fractions.
To be fully stand-alone, "combinatorial type" should be unpacked as a fixed face-incidence or face-lattice type of polytope.

The intended task is a realizability/classification problem: determine which collections of such sails can actually occur as the polytope varies over all lattice polytopes of the chosen combinatorial type.
refined_question: Fix one of the paper's sail constructions in the sense of Definition 2.2 for cones in R^n with lattice Z^n. For a fixed combinatorial type of lattice polytope (that is, a fixed face-lattice type), determine exactly which collections of sails of the polytope's vertex cones can occur as the polytope ranges over all lattice polytopes of that combinatorial type.
justification: The draft is targeting Section 3.3, Problem 8, almost verbatim: that is the only nearby official problem whose wording asks to "describe the collections of the sails of the cones for all polytopes of a given combinatorial type." I therefore kept the scope at Problem 8 and did not broaden it to neighboring questions about finite two-dimensional sails, periodic sails, or torus decompositions. To make the question stand alone while staying faithful to the paper, I added only the nearby context the paper itself supplies: the general definition of sail from Definition 2.2, the ambient lattice setting, the rational/finite context of Section 3.1, and the comparison with Problem 2 showing that the relevant cones are the multidimensional analogue of vertex angles.
